title: Should every Mark III be allowed to buy the starting brain?
question:
Recommend letting every Mark III buy the starting brain now for 200 gold. It replaces the robot's current brain with one the studio trained on 96 practice farms, then the robot continues learning each night. On 24 unfamiliar farms, it gained about one point a day in its first week on open ground (19.8 against 18.8 for a robot starting from nothing), and 0.5 to 1.1 on assigned squares. Most of that gain came in the first three days.

The current shelf only lets a robot with no completed night buy the starting brain. A robot that had learned for a week lost its farm-specific learning after the replacement and then did slightly worse the next week (29.3 points a day against 30.1). Letting every Mark III buy the starting brain accepts that trade-off.

The game records replayable days, and replaying one can rebuild the farm and what the robot could see at each recorded action. Whether those records can effectively train a replacement brain back toward a particular farm is not known. Training from saved days is not built and requires implementation and measurement before it can be offered as a later improvement. It does not delay this sale.
why_now: It is built and on the shelf now, with both test suites passing. The price is a placeholder for playtesting, so nothing is blocked while this waits.

options.label: Let every Mark III buy the starting brain now (Recommended)
options.detail: Any Mark III can buy the trained starting brain. A robot that has already learned loses what it learned on your farm, and in testing it did slightly worse afterwards.

options.label: Keep the starting brain for a new Mark III only
options.detail: Sold for 200 gold, only to a Mark III that has not yet had a night. A robot that has learned on your farm keeps its own learning.

options.label: Make it cheaper, since it only helps a little
options.detail: Drop the price to 50 gold, closer to what about a point a day for a week is worth.

options.label: Take it off the shelf until it clearly helps
options.detail: Keep the training tool and the purchase, but hide the card until a starting brain beats a robot starting from nothing on most farms.

links.caption: The shelf: the pace setting, and below it the starting brain for sale, a Mark III with a spark beside its head.
Bought: the price is gone and the spark turns brass, so the card keeps saying this robot started from the studio's brain.
A robot that has already had a night: the current build dims the card and will not take a tap.

replies.text:
I corrected the recommendation to match your direction: every Mark III can buy the starting brain now. The sale does not wait for replay-based refitting. A robot that has already learned still gives up its farm-specific learning and did slightly worse in the measured follow-up week.

A replay can rebuild the recorded farm and the robot's view at each action, but that does not show that saved days will train a replacement brain effectively. Replay-based refitting is a separate future improvement. It needs implementation and a measured comparison before we can say whether it restores useful farm-specific learning.
